method:
Best Bets: the strict card. Only plays from a rule that has ALREADY beaten the closing line in our own
graded history. Writes data/best_bets.json (rules scoreboard + daily cards + full history).

THE BAR (re-checked from the ledgers on every build, so a rule that stops working stops producing picks)
  A rule is one sport + market + minimum gap between our model and the line, e.g. "CBB totals, model 8+ pts
  off the line". Each is graded on every finished game in that sport's ledger, betting the model's side at
  the CLOSING line (the hardest number to beat). A rule qualifies only if ALL hold:
    1. n >= MIN_N graded games
    2. the lower end of the 95% confidence interval (Wilson) on its win rate is above 52.38% - the -110
       break-even - so the record is not just a hot streak
    3. it beats 52.38% in BOTH halves of its history (earlier and later games), so it isn't one good week
  Spreads only for leagues with real point spreads (NFL/NBA/CFB/CBB); NHL puck lines and MLB run lines are
  priced far from -110, so a W-L rate says nothing about them. Totals for every league with a ledger.
  About 30 rules are tested, so expect one to sneak through by luck now and then; condition 3 and the
  per-build re-check are the guard. First result (11/25/26): only CBB totals at 8+ points qualified
  (155-107, 59.2%, n=262; halves 56.5% / 61.8%).

TODAY'S PLAYS
  Every game today (PT day) whose current DraftKings line gives a qualifying rule's gap or more, model side.
  Out: DraftKings money at least 15 points heavier than tickets on the OTHER side (the one thing that can
  veto it; splits never add a play). At most MAX_PLAYS a day, biggest gaps first. Flat FLAT_U units each:
  the bar is about whether the edge is real, not how big.
  Timing (same clock as YAK's card): until 1 PM PT the qualifiers show as "On watch" (unofficial, lines
  still moving). A play on a game tipping before 1 PM locks about LOCK_MIN minutes before tip; the first
  build at/after 1 PM locks the rest, and the card never changes after that. Graded at the price taken,
  with closing-line value, by YAK's grader.
